answers.question: List of scenarios
answers.answer:
Three scenario frameworks were used:
1. Scenario 1 – Orderly Transition (modelled global temperature increase: 1.4°C; international archetype: NGFS – Orderly, RCP 1.9, SSP1: Sustainability, CCC: Tailwinds, IEA: NZE)
2. Scenario 2 – Disorderly Transition (modelled global temperature increase: 1.6°C; international archetype: NGFS – Disorderly, RCP 2.6, SSP1: Sustainability, CCC: Tailwinds, IEA: SDS)
3. Scenario 3 – Hot House (modelled global temperature increase: >3.0°C; international archetype: NGFS – Hot House, RCP 8.5, SSP5: Fossil Fuel Development, CCC: Current Policy Reference, IEA: STEPS)
answers.evidence: Scenario Framework and Parameters | Scenario 1 Orderly Transition | Scenario 2 Disorderly Transition | Scenario 3 Hot House | Modelled global temperature increase: 1.4°C | 1.6°C | >3.0°C ... International Scenario Archetype: NGFS – Orderly RCP 1.9 SSP1: Sustainability CCC: Tailwinds IEA: NZE | NGFS – Disorderly RCP 2.6 SSP1: Sustainability CCC: Tailwinds IEA: SDS | NGFS – Hot House RCP 8.5 SSP5: Fossil Fuel Development CCC: Current Policy Reference IEA: STEPS
answers.notes: Three time horizons were used for each scenario: short (2024–2030), medium (2030–2040), and long (2040–2050).

answers.question: Pick-and-mix of SSPs and RCPs
answers.answer:
The document pairs the following SSPs and RCPs across its three scenarios:
- Scenario 1 (Orderly Transition): RCP 1.9 + SSP1: Sustainability
- Scenario 2 (Disorderly Transition): RCP 2.6 + SSP1: Sustainability
- Scenario 3 (Hot House): RCP 8.5 + SSP5: Fossil Fuel Development
answers.evidence: "NGFS – Orderly RCP 1.9 SSP1: Sustainability ... NGFS – Disorderly RCP 2.6 SSP1: Sustainability ... NGFS – Hot House RCP 8.5 SSP5: Fossil Fuel Development"
answers.notes: Notably, both the Orderly and Disorderly scenarios use SSP1: Sustainability but with different RCPs (1.9 and 2.6 respectively), while the Hot House scenario uses SSP5: Fossil Fuel Development with RCP 8.5.

answers.question: Customised scenarios
answers.answer: Yes. CMC developed three customised scenario narratives with an external consultant, in accordance with NZCS1 and NZCS3: (1) Orderly Transition (1.4°C, cohesive & immediate global policy, aligned regional policy, hastened & high-cost technological change, low physical risks, moderate-high transition risks); (2) Disorderly Transition (1.6°C, reactive & inconsistent global policy, inconsistent regional policy, sporadic then quickening technological change, low-moderate physical risks, high transition risks); and (3) Hot House (>3.0°C, minimal & consumer-driven global policy, self-interest regional policy, market-driven & low-cost technological change, high physical risks, low transition risks). Narratives were mapped across three time horizons: short (2024–2030), medium (2030–2040), and long (2040–2050).
answers.evidence: "The Company engaged an external consultant to assist the Management team to establish customised scenario narratives for CMC in accordance with NZCS1 and NZCS3. These were then presented to the Board for their consideration and approval. The three scenario frameworks are summarised in the table below. Narratives (hypothetical pathways of plausible actions) were mapped out for each scenario framework using three time horizons: short (2024-2030), medium (2030-2040) and long (2040-2050)."
answers.location_hint: Climate Statement June 2024, page 2, Scenario Analysis Process section
answers.notes: The three scenarios align with international archetypes: Scenario 1 (NGFS Orderly, RCP 1.9, SSP1, CCC Tailwinds, IEA NZE), Scenario 2 (NGFS Disorderly, RCP 2.6, SSP1, CCC Tailwinds, IEA SDS), Scenario 3 (NGFS Hot House, RCP 8.5, SSP5, CCC Current Policy Reference, IEA STEPS).

answers.question: Co-produced climate scenarios
answers.answer: CMC participated in the Transport Sector Climate Scenarios Working Group during 2023-24, which aimed to develop an integrated set of scenarios across the transport sector. CMC maintained consistency with the Working Group by using the same time horizons. However, the outputs of the Working Group were not available when CMC undertook its customised analysis. CMC also engaged an external consultant to assist Management in establishing customised scenario narratives in accordance with NZCS1 and NZCS3, which were then presented to the Board for consideration and approval.
answers.evidence:
"During 2023-24, Management participated in the Transport Sector Climate Scenarios Working Group whose aim was to develop an integrated set of scenarios across the transport sector. The CMC scenario analysis process maintained consistency with the transport sector by using the same time horizons as the Working Group. Although the outputs of the Working Group were not available when CMC undertook its customised analysis, the Company's scenario frameworks are similar to those used by the Working Group."

"The Company engaged an external consultant to assist the Management team to establish customised scenario narratives for CMC in accordance with NZCS1 and NZCS3. These were then presented to the Board for their consideration and approval."
answers.notes: CMC co-produced scenarios with an external consultant and participated in the Transport Sector Climate Scenarios Working Group, though the Working Group's outputs were not yet available at the time CMC completed its own analysis. The scenario frameworks are described as similar to those used by the Working Group.

answers.question: Damage from acute physical risk considered
answers.answer: Yes. CMC considers damage from acute physical risks including worsening weather events and severe weather-related supply chain disruptions. Assets can be physically impacted by climate change, incurring costs to prevent or repair damage. Risks are mitigated by geographical spread of assets, and most assets are in urban commercial areas that would benefit from community-based mitigation (e.g. flood control works). In the current financial year, there were no known physical impacts of climate change that materially affected the Group.
answers.evidence: "Assets can be physically impacted by climate change. This is likely to incur costs to prevent or repair damage. Worsening weather events, or chronic impacts for example sea level change, have the potential to increase the cost of asset ownership or decrease the value of property." and "In the current financial year, there were no known physical impacts of climate change that materially affected the Group."
answers.notes: The document addresses both acute physical risks (worsening weather events, severe weather disruptions to supply chains) and chronic physical risks (sea level change). No material physical damage was recorded in the current financial year.

answers.question: Non-temperature variables in scenarios
answers.answer: The scenarios include the following non-temperature variables: Global policy reaction, Regional policy variation, Speed of technological change, Consumer sentiment/behaviour change, Physical risks severity, Transition risks severity, and National vehicle fleet composition.

answers.question: Time frames
answers.answer: CMC uses three time horizons for scenario analysis: short (2024–2030), medium (2030–2040), and long (2040–2050). For risk and opportunity assessment, the time frames used are short to mid-term (2024–2040), excluding the longer-term horizon to align with CMC's risk assessment time frames. In the annual strategic risk review, short to mid-term risks cover the next five years and mid to long-term risks cover five to ten years.

answers.question: Justification for scenario/model choice
answers.answer: CMC chose three scenario frameworks (Orderly Transition, Disorderly Transition, and Hot House) aligned with international archetypes including NGFS, RCP, SSP, CCC, and IEA scenarios. The justification provided is that: (1) the scenarios were developed with an external consultant in accordance with NZCS1 and NZCS3; (2) CMC participated in the Transport Sector Climate Scenarios Working Group and maintained consistency with the transport sector by using the same time horizons; and (3) although the Working Group's outputs were not available when CMC undertook its analysis, the Company's scenario frameworks are similar to those used by the Working Group.

The CMC scenario analysis process maintained consistency with the transport sector by using the same time horizons as the Working Group. answers.question: Historic climate impacts
answers.answer: In the current financial year (2024), there were no known physical impacts of climate change that materially affected the Group. There were a number of transitional impacts (e.g. political, economic, technological, social), the most influential of which was the end of the Clean Car Discount and Tax regime.
answers.evidence: "In the current financial year, there were no known physical impacts of climate change that materially affected the Group. There were a number of transitional impacts (e.g. political, economic, technological, social). The most influential of these transitional impacts was the end of the Clean Car Discount and Tax regime. This shifted sales timings within the year and affected demand for some products, particularly Low Emission Vehicles (LEV's) and Light Commercial Vehicles."
answers.location_hint: Climate Statement June 2024.pdf, page 1, Section 2 (Strategy – Current Material Impacts)
answers.notes: The document explicitly states no material physical climate impacts occurred in the reporting year, but identifies the end of the Clean Car Discount and Tax regime as the most influential transitional impact.

answers.question: Direct and indirect physical climate risks
answers.answer:
CMC identifies the following physical climate risks:

1. **Direct physical risk – Property and vehicle stocks**: Assets can be physically impacted by climate change, incurring costs to prevent or repair damage. Worsening weather events, or chronic impacts such as sea level change, have the potential to increase the cost of asset ownership or decrease the value of property. Risks are mitigated by the Company's geographical spread of assets, and most assets are within urban commercial areas which would likely benefit from community-based mitigation (e.g. flood control works). Insurance premiums and council rates are likely to continue to increase.

2. **Indirect physical risk – Supply chain disruptions**: New Zealand supply chains can be disrupted due to severe weather events, or by repairs or strengthening work associated with storm damage or mitigation/adaptation programmes. International supply chains and logistics to New Zealand can also be disrupted by physical events and changes to shipping routes and methods.

In the current financial year (2024), there were no known physical impacts of climate change that materially affected the Group.
answers.evidence:
"Property and vehicle stocks (physical): Assets can be physically impacted by climate change. This is likely to incur costs to prevent or repair damage. Worsening weather events, or chronic impacts for example sea level change, have the potential to increase the cost of asset ownership or decrease the value of property. • Risks are mitigated by the Company's geographical spread of assets. • Most assets are within urban commercial areas which mean they would likely benefit from any community-based mitigation, e.g. flood control works. • Insurance premiums and council rates are likely to continue to increase."

"Supply chain disruptions (transitional): New Zealand supply chains can be disrupted due to severe weather events, or by the repairs or strengthening work associated with storm damage or mitigation/adaption programmes. International supply chains and logistics to New Zealand can be disrupted by physical events. They can also be impacted by changes to shipping routes and methods."

"In the current financial year, there were no known physical impacts of climate change that materially affected the Group."
answers.notes: Supply chain disruptions are labelled as "transitional" in the document but include physical sub-risks (severe weather events, physical disruptions to international logistics). The document explicitly categorises "Property and vehicle stocks" as a physical risk. The scenario analysis also notes physical risks severity ranges from Low (Orderly Transition) to High (Hot House scenario).
